title: NFL Holds Off Reinstating Brandon Aiyuk from Reserve/Left Squad List, NBC Sports Reports
body:
The San Francisco 49ers have yet to approve wide‑receiver Brandon Aiyuk’s request to return to the active roster after he was placed on the reserve/left squad list in early October, a procedural snag that has left the team’s offensive game plan in limbo and sparked speculation about the league’s internal processes.

Aiyuk, who entered the season as a key component of the 49ers’ passing attack, filed the requisite paperwork to be reinstated last week. Despite the seemingly straightforward nature of the request, the NFL’s administrative machinery has not completed the clearance, and the player remains ineligible to practice or suit up for upcoming games. The delay has prompted questions from analysts and fans alike about why a routine roster move is dragging out, especially given the 49ers’ recent injury woes at the receiver position.

The reserve/left squad list is typically used when a player steps away from the team for personal reasons, allowing the franchise to retain his rights while freeing a roster spot. Once the player is ready to return, the team files a reinstatement request, which the league must approve before the athlete can rejoin team activities. In most cases, the process is completed within a few days. However, in Aiyuk’s situation, the paperwork appears to have hit an administrative bottleneck, possibly involving verification of medical documentation, compliance with the league’s personal‑leave policy, or a simple clerical oversight.

The timing could not be more consequential for San Francisco. The 49ers have been dealing with a spate of injuries to their receiving corps, including the loss of Deebo Samuel to a hamstring strain and a lingering ankle issue for Jauan Jennings. Aiyuk, who posted 71 receptions for 1,037 yards and six touchdowns last season, is viewed as the most reliable option to keep the offense balanced while quarterback Brock Purdy continues to navigate a demanding schedule. Without Aiyuk’s presence, the 49ers have been forced to rely heavily on younger, less experienced players and on tight ends like George Kittle to fill the void, a strategy that has yielded mixed results.

From a broader perspective, the episode underscores the growing complexity of roster management in the modern NFL. Teams now juggle a myriad of contractual clauses, health protocols, and personal‑leave provisions that can complicate even routine transactions. The league has faced criticism in recent years for opaque procedures and inconsistent communication regarding player status changes. While the NFL’s operations department has not commented publicly on the specific delay, insiders suggest that the league is reviewing its internal workflows to prevent similar hiccups from affecting other high‑profile players.

For Aiyuk, the uncertainty is more than a bureaucratic inconvenience. The wide receiver has expressed a strong desire to rejoin his teammates and contribute on the field, emphasizing his commitment to the organization and his readiness to play. Teammates have voiced support on social media, with several players noting that his return would boost morale and provide a much‑needed spark to a unit that has struggled to find rhythm in recent weeks.

Looking ahead, the 49ers will need to adapt quickly regardless of the outcome. If the league clears Aiyuk within the next few days, he could be activated in time for the team’s upcoming matchup against the Arizona Cardinals, a game that could serve as a litmus test for the offense’s resilience. Conversely, if the reinstatement is further delayed, San Francisco may have to explore alternative options, such as promoting a practice‑squad player or seeking a short‑term trade. Either scenario will force the coaching staff to recalibrate their strategy as the regular season pushes toward its critical stretch. The resolution of Aiyuk’s reinstatement will therefore not only affect one player’s career trajectory but also shape the 49ers’ pursuit of a playoff berth in the weeks to come.
